the inscription of the Shi Qiang pan E34: Inscription dynastic genealogy E55: Type
Chinese E56: Language
[Description] The text first praises the previous and current rulers of the Zhou dynasty, extolling their virtues and deeds, recording the virtues and highlights of the first seven Zhou kings; it then recounts the history of the family of the caster, culminating with Scribe Qiang himself. This is in contrast to most bronze inscriptions, which detail only immediate events. [Statement] The article names only three of the seven kings — Wen, Wu and Zhao — and states that the current ruler is praised; the reigning king at the time of casting was King Gong. The remaining kings are not named in the article and are not modelled here. [Statement] The language of the inscription is difficult both graphically and lexically. Transcriptions are available, but most are incomplete due to font constraints.

[Made Note] The article says the vessel "was cast ... for a member of the Wei clan whose name was Qiang" and elsewhere calls Qiang "the caster". Qiang is therefore recorded here as the actor of the production in the role of the patron for whom, and in whose name, the vessel was cast — the conventional sinological sense of "caster". The bronze-worker who physically cast the vessel is not named in the article.
